licenses.text:
Biblia Takatifu, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/swh1850/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this translation):
> "Public Domain
Language: Kiswahili (Swahili)
Dialect: Kimvita
Translation by: Dr. Johann Ludvig Krapf"
(from eBible.org's page for this translation, https://ebible.org/swh1850/copyright.htm)

Why this is public domain:
Translator: Johann Ludwig Krapf, 1810-1881, a German missionary in East Africa; eBible says his translation of portions of the New Testament was completed in 1850. US: a work published before 1931 is public domain in the United States, and a work left unpublished is public domain there 70 years after its author's death (Krapf's ended in 1951). Origin country: Krapf lived until 1881, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 140 years or less, whatever its country of first publication. Nobody besides Krapf is named for this text.

Sources of these facts:
eBible.org copyright page (https://ebible.org/swh1850/copyright.htm) and details page (https://ebible.org/details.php?id=swh1850); Krapf's life dates from English Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Ludwig_Krapf).

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

note: The verse-numbered twin of ebible-swh1850-510b1410, for the parallel verses measure only (#35): its tag is verse-numbers alone, which no mixture selects, so it never enters training. eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside.
